with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. Every question on this page
has its answer: try first, then check.

## Key terms

{{< glossary conditional-probability dependent-events independent-events multiplication-rule tree-diagram random-variable expected-value fair-game >}}

## 14.1 Conditional probability

- **P(A | B) = P(A and B) / P(B)**: the probability of A when B is known.
- Count A **only inside B**, divide by the outcomes of B.
- A door opens with a sum ≥ 10, and the first die is a 6: 3 of 6 → 1/2
  (without the condition: 1/6).

![P(A | B): count only inside B.](images/conditional-grid.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/conditional-lab.html" poster="sims/conditional-lab.png" title="Conditional Lab: what do we know already?" height="740" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
After a condition, divide by the outcomes of B, not by 36.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Count inside B"}
Find P(sum 7 | first die is 1), P(a double | the sum is even), and P(sum ≥
10 | at least one 6).

::: {.check}
1/6 (only (1, 6)); 6/18 = 1/3 (18 even sums, 6 doubles); 5/11 ((4,6),
(5,6), (6,4), (6,5), (6,6) of the 11 outcomes with a 6).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Conditions"}
Use Conditional Lab. Choose the probability.

::: {.match extra="1/36|5/36"}
Two dice, the first die is 6. What is P(sum ≥ 9)?
:   2/3

    Why: (6,3), (6,4), (6,5), (6,6): 4 of 6.

Two dice, at least one 6. What is P(a double)?
:   1/11

    Why: inside the 11 outcomes with a 6, only (6, 6).

Two dice, the sum is 4. What is P(a double)?
:   1/3

    Why: (1,3), (2,2), (3,1): one double of 3.

Two dice, the sum is 7. What is P(first die is 1)?
:   1/6

    Why: 6 pairs make 7, and only (1, 6) starts with 1.

Two dice, the first die is 4. What is P(sum ≥ 8)?
:   1/2

    Why: (4,4), (4,5), (4,6): 3 of 6.
:::
:::

## 14.2 Dependent events and the multiplication rule

- **P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B | A)**.
- **Dependent:** the first result changes the second (no putting back).
- Two storms of 12 cards with 3 storms: 3/12 × 2/11 = **1/22**.
- **Independent:** P(A | B) = P(A). Two dice are independent: the past of a
  die never changes its next roll.

![Two cards without putting the first back.](images/tree-no-return.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Without putting back, the second fraction changes: 2/11, not 3/12.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · A deck of quests"}
10 quest cards, 4 easy. Two draws without putting back: P(two easy), P(easy
then hard).

::: {.check}
4/10 × 3/9 = 2/15; 4/10 × 6/9 = 4/15.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Two draws"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="2/12|dependent"}
6 cards, 2 red. Two draws, no putting back. What is P(two red)?
:   1/15

    Why: 2/6 × 1/5 = 2/30.

6 cards, 2 red. Two draws, the card is put back. What is P(two red)?
:   1/9

    Why: 1/3 × 1/3: the deck is the same for the second draw.

9 quests, 3 easy. Two draws, no putting back. What is P(two easy)?
:   1/12

    Why: 3/9 × 2/8 = 6/72.

Two dice: are "sum 7" and "first die is 6" independent?
:   independent

    Why: P(sum 7 | first die 6) = 1/6 = P(sum 7).

5 keys, 1 gold. Two draws, no putting back. What is P(gold, then not gold)?
:   1/5

    Why: 1/5 × 4/4: after the gold key, every key left is not gold.
:::
:::

## 14.3 Random variables and the expected value

- A **random variable**: a number that depends on chance (coins, damage).
- **E = x₁p₁ + x₂p₂ + …**: the long-run average.
- Crate: 100·0.1 + 20·0.3 + 5·0.6 = **19 coins**.

![The expected value of a loot crate.](images/expected-value.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/crate-lab.html" poster="sims/crate-lab.png" title="Crate Lab: the expected value of a loot crate" height="800" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
(100 + 20 + 5) / 3 is not E: the probabilities are missing.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Two crates"}
Open 1000 crates in **Crate Lab**. Then compute E for gold 50 (2/10), silver
20 (3/10), wood 0 (5/10).

::: {.check}
After 1000 crates the average is close to 19. E = 10 + 6 + 0 = 16 coins.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Expected values"}
Choose E.

::: {.match extra="41.7|125"}
30 coins (0.5) or 10 coins (0.5)?
:   20

    Why: 15 + 5.

20 damage (0.6) or 5 damage (0.4)?
:   14

    Why: 12 + 2.

40 coins (0.25) or nothing (0.75)?
:   10

    Why: 40 × 0.25 = 10; nothing adds 0.

4 (0.5), 0 (0.3) or 10 (0.2)?
:   4

    Why: 2 + 0 + 2.

100 coins (0.05) or nothing (0.95)?
:   5

    Why: 100 × 0.05 = 5.
:::
:::

## 14.4 Fair games and the number of tries

- **Expected gain = E(win) − price.** Fair: gain 0.
- Pay 2, win 10 on a 6: 1.67 − 2 ≈ −0.33. Fair price 1.67.
- Success with probability p: on average **1/p** tries.

![A fair price and the average number of tries.](images/fair-game.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
1/p is an average: after 10 crates with p = 1/10, about 35 % still have no
gold.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Fair or not?"}
A spinner with 8 parts; one wins 20 coins; a spin costs 3. Fair? Fair price?
Average spins to win?

::: {.check}
E(win) = 20/8 = 2.5; gain −0.5: not fair. Fair price 2.5 coins. On average
8 spins.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Fair games"}
Use Crate Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="+3 coins|100"}
Pay 1 coin, win 3 coins on a 5 or a 6. The expected gain?
:   0 coins

    Why: E(win) = 3 × 2/6 = 1; 1 − 1 = 0: fair.

A crate has E = 12 coins. Which price is fair?
:   12 coins

    Why: fair means the price equals E(win).

A drop chance of 1/20. How many crates on average?
:   20

    Why: 1/p.

A spinner with 5 parts; one wins 10. Which price is fair?
:   2 coins

    Why: E(win) = 10 × 1/5 = 2.

Pay 4 coins; 1 of 4 parts wins 12. The expected gain?
:   −1 coin

    Why: E(win) = 12 × 1/4 = 3; 3 − 4.
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Treasure Odds {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

The designer of *Lucky Raft* tunes the loot drops and the critical hits of
its dungeon. A **critical hit** needs a sum of 11 or more on two dice, and
the first die already shows a 5. A **chest** holds 8 items, 2 of them rare,
and the hero takes two. An **enemy** drops 50 coins (1/10), 10 coins (4/10)
or nothing (5/10). A normal hit does 10 damage, and a **critical hit**
(probability 1/4) does 30. A **lucky wheel** costs 3 coins and one of its 10
parts wins 20 coins. A **rare pet** drops with probability 1/25.

{{< sim file="sims/treasure-odds.html" poster="sims/treasure-odds.png" title="Treasure Odds: loot drops and critical hits" kind="game" height="460" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Loot and hits"}
The dungeon: critical hit sum ≥ 11, first die 5; chest 8 items, 2 rare;
enemy 50 (1/10), 10 (4/10), 0 (5/10); wheel 3 coins, 1 of 10 parts wins 20;
pet 1/25. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="1/12|1/16"}
P(critical hit), knowing the first die is 5?
:   1/6

    Why: only (5, 6) of the 6 cases reaches 11.

P(two rare items) from the chest?
:   1/28

    Why: 2/8 × 1/7: the first item stays out.

Expected coins per enemy?
:   9

    Why: 5 + 4 + 0.

Expected gain per spin of the wheel?
:   −1 coin

    Why: E(win) = 2; 2 − 3.

Enemies on average for one pet?
:   25

    Why: 1/p.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Tune the hits (harder)"}
A normal hit does 10 damage; a critical hit has probability 1/4. Choose the
right answer.

::: {.match extra="40|always 4 hits"}
A critical hit does 30. What is E(damage) per hit?
:   15

    Why: 10 × 3/4 + 30 × 1/4 = 7.5 + 7.5.

The designer wants E(damage) = 20. How much must a critical hit do?
:   50

    Why: 7.5 + x/4 = 20, so x/4 = 12.5.

On average, how many hits until the first critical hit?
:   4

    Why: 1/p = 1 ÷ 1/4.

Is a critical hit after 3 normal hits more likely than 1/4?
:   no, still 1/4

    Why: the hits are independent: the past does not change the next one.

The critical hit does 30, and its chance becomes 1/2. What is E(damage)?
:   20

    Why: 10 × 1/2 + 30 × 1/2 = 5 + 15.
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- P(A | B): count A only inside B.
- P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B | A); without putting back, the branches change.
- Independent: P(A | B) = P(A); the past of a die does not change its next roll.
- E = Σ value × probability: the long-run average.
- Fair: expected gain 0. Average tries: 1/p.
